chunks: By Allah, this is the case of right with the rightful person, and I do not care what the heretics do; and that is an end to the matter.

key_terms.الْمُلِحِدُونَ: The heretics or those who deviate from the truth
key_terms.مُحِقٍّ: The one who possesses the truth/right

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali mean by 'right with the rightful' in his letter to Abu Musa?
ai.summary: In this letter to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) contrasts the steadfastness of the righteous with the fluctuating loyalty of the Kharijites and early opponents, emphasizing that divine truth remains with those who uphold justice regardless of external political pressures. The phrase 'what do I care what the heretics do' reflects the Shia scholarly view of *al-mulhidun* not merely as doctrinal deviants but as those who distort reality for political gain, a key theme in Ali's governance. This assertion serves as a theological anchor for the concept of *Haqq* (Truth/Right) being objective and independent of popular opinion or administrative convenience.
